tested_scope.mechanism: deterministic operation-key path used as a create-only idempotency receipt/tombstone
tested_scope.prior_observation_reused: same-path create-only retry is rejected while the path remains present
tested_scope.new_question: Does that property establish ABA-resistant retry suppression when the design promises append-only retention?
tested_scope.reason_destructive_test_not_required_for: The transport surface itself exposes file deletion as a mutation capability; therefore path-presence exclusion cannot by itself enforce the retention invariant. This slice tests the logical boundary of the append-only design, not destructive behavior.

result.conditional_design_property: If every committed operation-key receipt/tombstone is retained permanently and no actor can delete or replace the key path, then the previously observed create-only same-path exclusion suppresses duplicate creation for that key across retries while the retention invariant holds.
result.retention_assumption: A committed operation-key receipt/tombstone must remain present for the full lifetime in which the key may be replayed; delete/recreate and path replacement are forbidden for all actors that can affect the namespace.
result.transport_reason: The available GitHub contents mutation surface includes deletion and replacement/update operations, so the transport does not itself make the operation-key path write-once or non-deletable.
result.aba_state_transition: If deletion returns the deterministic key path to the absent state, the create-only precondition is re-opened and a later replay can be accepted as a new create. Therefore the same-path collision property alone does not prove ABA resistance.
result.hard_gate_resolution: conditional retry suppression under an external append-only retention invariant; unconditional ABA resistance remains unresolved because retention is not transport-enforced
